summary: Ilulissat Airport serves as the main aerial gateway to the Ilulissat Icefjord, a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its massive calving glaciers. Located on the west coast of Greenland, just a few kilometers from the town of Ilulissat, the airport plays a vital role in connecting this remote Arctic community to Nuuk, Kangerlussuaq, and Reykjavik. Operations are dominated by regional turboprop flights adapted to the demanding polar environment.
faqs:
Q: How do I get from Ilulissat Airport to the town?
A: The airport is only about 5 minutes by road from Ilulissat town center. Taxis typically wait outside the small terminal, and most hotels offer pre-arranged pickup services.

Q: Which airlines operate flights to Ilulissat?
A: Air Greenland is the primary carrier, offering scheduled service from Kangerlussuaq and Nuuk, as well as seasonal international flights from Reykjavik in Iceland.

Q: When is the best time to visit Ilulissat?
A: Summer (June to August) brings the midnight sun and excellent iceberg viewing
